title: CFL: Causally Fair Language Models Through Token-level Attribute Controlled Generation
benchmark_measurement: The paper measures unintended bias and toxicity associated with religious identity terms. It specifically evaluates whether detoxification methods unfairly penalize or over-filter text containing names of protected religious groups (e.g., Muslims) due to spurious correlations in the training data. The proposed 'Causally Fair Language' (CFL) model uses Average Treatment Effect (ATE) scores to isolate the causal contribution of each token to toxicity, aiming to understand that terms like 'Muslims' are not inherently hateful.
findings: The paper found that its proposed causal method (CFL) can successfully mitigate unintended bias against protected religious groups that often arises during model detoxification. By computing token-level Average Treatment Effect (ATE) scores, the model learns to decouple identity terms like 'Muslims' or 'Christians' from toxic attributes. For instance, it correctly identifies that the term 'Muslims' itself is not the cause of hatefulness in a sentence. This approach leads to a lower performance drop (loss gap) on sentences containing protected group terms compared to other detoxification methods, indicating less harmful over-filtering.
